correctness.rationale: For n>=1 and r>=3, the quotient bijection from an exact meet partition to r partitions with discrete quotient meet gives T(r,k)=sum_j s(k,j)B_j^r. Independently chosen Boolean valuations on a cell of size m yield Phi_m(z)=1+(1+z)^m-z^m. Multiplication and averaging give the exact generating polynomial. Each pair-collision event has probability (B[n-1]/B[n])^r and any pair of distinct events has intersection probability (B[n-2]/B[n])^r. Independent fair valuations separate two (even overlapping) pairs with joint probability 1/4, proving both Bonferroni bounds. Their relative error is bounded by (N-1)/2(B[n-2]/B[n-1])^3=O(W0(n)^3/n) uniformly for all integers r>=3. The single-doubleton event follows because two simultaneous pair events imply a second-order collision; on it, exactly one world can violate p->Dp. The Lambert-W replacement of Bell ratios is restricted to fixed r. Exact independent finite checks at six (n,r) points, including all valuations, returned ALL_CHECKS_OK; the infinite proof is symbolic.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The counting coefficient T(r,k) is immediately implied by Pittel/Canfield, and the uniform fixed-r three-agent discrete-meet tendency is also known. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A finite S5 equivalence relation is a labelled set partition and the accessibility relation for distributed knowledge is its meet. Quotienting by the meet gives exactly the classical discrete-meet count T(r,k). Thus frame-level unmarked probability, including the probability of an identity meet, is prior work. The new statistic additionally marks an independently sampled Boolean valuation, each nonconstant meet block contributing a number of violating worlds; neither cited theorem specifies this marked polynomial. The uniform r>=3 conditional one-doubleton and one-violating-world estimates follow from two-edge intersection and Bell-ratio inequalities not stated as results in inspected prior works.

originality.rationale: The old exact unmarked Bell-partition meet count and fixed-r trivial-meet tendency are fully credited to Pittel (2000) and Canfield (2001). The independently sampled truth-valuation failure-count generating polynomial, sharp detection probability and uniform agent-count first-defect/one-world failure law are the assessed additions. Full primary texts and linked tables were inspected; no explicitly covering statement was found. This is best-knowledge originality, not independently certified historical priority.
residual_risks: Canfield's general meet decomposition combined with a generic weighted Bell-polynomial transfer could imply the marked polynomial as a corollary not recognized by name.
A stronger unstated classical occupancy or collision sieve might directly imply the sharp uniform three-agent rare-defect rate.
Accessible published mathematical-research summaries are incomplete, so absence of a match is not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Counting the worlds that falsify p->Dp is a natural diagnostic of information loss in finite distributed-knowledge S5 frames. The result gives the entire finite probability distribution for every labelled world count and number of agents, distinguishes countermodel existence from detection by a sampled valuation, and supplies the sharp 3-agent failure coefficient and a uniform isolated-pair structural description. The answer is nontrivial for actual independent uniform Bell sampling and can benchmark random epistemic models. It neither asserts downstream significance nor extends to asynchronous histories or arbitrary random partition laws.
